summary: A reporter covers a September 10, 2023 Wellness Workshop at the Lincoln Community Health Center focused on preventative health screenings and check-ups. Speakers covered screening schedules, the cost savings of early detection, health literacy, wearable tech and telehealth, and accessibility barriers. Attendees' personal stories and personalized 'Health Roadmaps' illustrated how early screening changes outcomes.
one_line: A report on a Lincoln Community Health Center workshop promoting screenings, early detection, health literacy, technology and access for lifelong wellness.
key_facts: The Wellness Workshop took place on September 10, 2023, at the Lincoln Community Health Center in the city center.
Dr. Elizabeth Moreno, a primary care physician, said conditions from high blood pressure to certain cancers can be 'silent killers' that show no symptoms until advanced.
Dr. Moreno said women should start mammograms at age 40 and continue annually.
Dr. Moreno said both men and women at age 50 should begin considering colon cancer screenings.
Attendees such as Mark, a 48-year-old local librarian, received a personalized 'Health Roadmap' after a brief consultation, outlining screenings suited to age, gender and health status.
Health economist Laura Gibson said treating stage 1 breast cancer could be four times less costly than managing it at stage 4.
Sarah Jennings, a 54-year-old school teacher, discovered she was pre-diabetic during a routine check-up and avoided full diabetes through dietary changes and more physical activity.
Dr. James Peterson, a workshop facilitator, stressed health literacy, saying patients need to feel competent understanding health information and comfortable making informed decisions.
Interactive sessions included Q&A segments and myth-busting activities to break down medical jargon.
One session covered wearable technology for monitoring health parameters, and another showcased telehealth for virtual routine screenings.
Clara Davis, a single mother of two, said she lacks the means to travel for check-ups and that taking time off work is difficult.
Local health policymakers shared initiatives including mobile clinics for underserved areas and policies to mandate paid leave for medical screenings.
